transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Lena O., Marcus H., Priya S. (Redwood) - Tommy W., Asha P., Ryan M., Marta N. (Cygnus)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align on POC success criteria (latency SLOs, throughput targets, cost envelopes), workload sizing and traffic patterns, and the recommended deployment mode options (hosted, dedicated, private/on-prem). Customer emphasized security and data residency for parts of workload; wants a pragmatic pilot timeline (6-8 weeks) and benchmarking plan.

Topics Covered:
- POC acceptance criteria and KPIs
- Traffic profile and burstiness (batch vs real-time)
- Benchmarks (throughput, p95 latency, token cost) and methodology
- Deployment modes trade-offs and gating factors (latency, compliance, control)
- Timeline and required artifacts for pilot

Action items (brief): see metadata field for owners/dates.

Transcript Body:
00:00 Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to get aligned on the POC goals for the Cygnus energy assistant project, sound good?
00:08 Tommy Wu: Yeah thanks, Lena. We, big picture, want to be able to serve internal Ops chat and automated shift handovers, so latency matters but security matters more. We'll have surge patterns during outages.
00:22 Marcus Hale: Right, so what we typically do is define two buckets: control-plane sensitive inference that stays private, and more generic queries that can hit hosted. But let's walk through volumes and SLOs.
00:36 Asha Patel: Quick note — we can't allow cloud-hosted logs for flagged PII events. That rules out hosted for some endpoints unless we obfuscate at the edge.
00:49 Lena Ortiz: Understood. For the POC, we usually recommend a 6 week window: week 1-2 for baseline and trace collection, week 3-4 benchmarking and tuning, week 5-6 validation and runbook handoff. We can compress or expand depending on approvals.
01:02 Ryan Mercer: Does Redwood have a quant plan? We're sensitive to token cost, and we'll be running long prompts sometimes — firmware updates, diagnostic logs — 800-1,200 tokens typical.
01:15 Marcus Hale: We do. For these lengths we show different kernel and quantization profiles. For example, an 8-bit quantized 6B family might cut cost by ~3x with modest quality delta. The tradeoff is peak latency; quantized runs can add a couple of ms but usually still within p95 SLOs.
01:30 Marta Novak: Security — what about KMS integration and HSM? We need to show how keys are kept on-prem for private deployments.
01:39 Priya Singh: On Private we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM and ensure audit logs are exported to their SIEM. For Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via our KMS connectors — depends on contract.
01:52 Tommy Wu: OK so we need to define success criteria. From our side: p95 < 300ms for short queries (<=128 tokens), p95 < 800ms for long queries (<=1200 tokens), throughput 250 qps sustained for our pilot peak, and cost under $0.30 per 1k tokens effective — those are ballpark.
02:12 Lena Ortiz: Those are helpful targets. We should make two lanes for acceptance: performance (latency/throughput), and security/compliance (no plain-text replay to hosted logs, KMS, audit). Also a qualitative metric: human eval on hallucination rate below X on our prompt set.
02:33 Asha Patel: On traffic patterns — our daytime baseline is ~30 qps with bursts to 300 qps during incidents for 2-10 minute windows. Average token length depends on query type; also we have batch annotation backfills overnight.
02:48 Marcus Hale: Good. For bursty workloads we recommend Dedicated with burst capacity or Private if you need full control. Hosted can handle but you lose some guarantees and it may be costlier under sustained bursts. Also prefix/KV caching will reduce tokens for repeated context, that helps a lot for Ops follow-ups.
03:06 Ryan Mercer: Can you quantify cache benefits?
03:09 Marcus Hale: Roughly, if 40% of requests share a prefix — say same incident description — we often see token cost reduction of 20-40% and lowered latency because KV cache avoids recomputing earlier layers. But it depends on your prompt reuse.
03:28 Tommy Wu: Ok, for POC we will provide a week's worth of traces (anonymized) so you can model real prefix reuse.
03:34 Lena Ortiz: Perfect. For benchmarks we propose: baseline throughput runs (steady-state 10m windows at 50, 100, 250 qps), spike tests (sudden jump to 300 qps for 10 min), and token-length sweeps (32/128/512/1024/1200). We'll run hosted vs dedicated vs private variants and capture p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, and cost per effective token.
03:58 Asha Patel: On-hosted vs dedicated versus private decision criteria — let's talk: If we pick hosted we get fastest time to market but less control. Dedicated gives predictable latency and isolation. Private satisfies our regulator but is a heavy lift for ops.
04:14 Marcus Hale: Exactly. Our recommended decision rubric: If you need audit/log residency + KMS w/ HSM -> Private. If you need predictable high sustained throughput with SLAs but don't want on-prem ops -> Dedicated. If you need fast experimentation and can accept token-level retention policies -> Hosted.
04:33 Marta Novak: For private, what's the expected on-prem effort? How many FTEs?
04:38 Priya Singh: Typical on-prem POC requires 1-2 Cygnus infra engineers for networking and firewall windows, and we provide an engineer from Redwood for installation and tuning for 2-3 weeks. If air-gapped, add more time for offline approvals and HSM attestations.
04:54 Ryan Mercer: Licensing and cost proforma?
04:57 Lena Ortiz: We'll share a dedicated vs private cost proforma that breaks out infra, support, and software fees. For Dedicated we usually have reserved capacity commitments with burst. For Private there's a platform license + professional services.
05:10 Tommy Wu: Let's include a gating rule: if the pilot shows >20% user-facing latency regressions versus current baseline, we pause rollout.
05:18 Marcus Hale: Fair. We'll instrument synthetic canaries and real-user metrics. Also we'll set up token-level cost logging so you can attribute spend by route.
05:29 Asha Patel: We need SOC2 + ISO evidence.
05:33 Lena Ortiz: We'll share SOC2 Type II attestation and our ISO summary pack. For deeper reviews, we can schedule a security review call.
05:41 Marta Novak: Also SAML SSO and RBAC for the console — needed.
05:45 Priya Singh: Supported. We'll map role templates to your org roles and integrate with SAML/SCIM.
05:52 Ryan Mercer: About benchmarking environments — will Redwood spin up a dedicated cluster in our cloud account for Dedicated tests or emulate on your side?
05:59 Marcus Hale: For Dedicated we can provision a trial pool in Redwood-managed infra or in your cloud under a trial subscription depending on procurement. For Private we'd deploy to your VPC. We'll detail options in the SOW.
06:14 Tommy Wu: Timeline alignment: we want an internal decision by mid-Jan, so POC needs to complete by end of December to give us time for procurement. Is that feasible?
06:24 Lena Ortiz: Tight but doable. If you can get traces by Dec 3 and sign the SOW by Dec 10 we can run a compressed 4 week pilot and deliver results by Dec 31.
06:35 Asha Patel: Procurement internal cycles — we'll try.
06:37 Marcus Hale: Technical note — when we run throughput benchmarks, we'll include tests with and without KV cache, and with quantized vs fp16 models. That'll give you a matrix of latency vs cost.
06:50 Ryan Mercer: Great. Also please include failure-mode tests: what happens when region capacity is constrained? We need automatic fallbacks.
06:58 Priya Singh: Redwood supports smart routing and fallback to compatible variants or regions; we'll document expected failover times and behavior.
07:08 Tommy Wu: Any external compliance vendors we should expect? Our legal team might want a pen-test and a supply chain questionnaire.
07:15 Lena Ortiz: We can coordinate pen-test windows and provide a vendor questionnaire template.
07:20 Marta Novak: Last thing — can we get an example SLO dashboard view?
07:24 Marcus Hale: I'll share a sample dashboard (latency, tokens per route, cost, and error breakdown).
07:29 Lena Ortiz: OK let's recap next steps: Marcus to run baseline tests (deliver Dec 3); Lena to send SOW and cost proforma (Dec 2); Cygnus to send anonymized traces and VPC topology (Dec 3); Security Qs from Marta by Dec 4. Schedule security deep dive week of Dec 6.
07:50 Tommy Wu: Sounds good, thank you all.
07:54 Asha Patel: Thanks.
07:56 Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and calendar invites.
08:02 End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: Portions of technical terms transcribed imperfectly — e.g., K V cache sometimes appears as KV cash, certain model names truncated. There is occasional crosstalk and filler words.
